record.name: Goran Žigić
record.title: Assistant Professor
record.department: Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics)
record.bio: Goran Žigić received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2008 and his PhD from the same institution in 2015, with a thesis on pressure-recovery instability in proportional hydraulic spool valves. He joined the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences as a Teaching Assistant in 2010 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on coupled CFD–FEM simulation of hydraulic control components, with particular interest in spool oscillation, cavitation erosion, and flow-induced noise at metering edges. Teaching duties include fluid mechanics, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, and numerical methods in engineering. The group regularly uses ANSYS Fluent, OpenFOAM, and an in-house hydraulic test rig equipped with high-speed pressure transducers and a laser Doppler anemometer.
open_to: contract research on hydraulic component simulation and testing
joint projects with hydraulic machinery manufacturers
consulting on cavitation damage assessment and valve noise reduction
student internships for mechanical or mechatronics engineering students
equipment access (hydraulic test rig, LDA system)
record.industry_experience: Žigić collaborated with Metaloprojekt Hidraulika d.o.o. during the VALVENOISE project and provided consulting on a directional valve redesign for a construction equipment manufacturer based in Zrenjanin. He is familiar with the constraints of manufacturing-oriented valve development.
record.notes: Žigić is interested in partnerships with companies at NTP Novi Sad working on fluid power components, mechatronic systems, or precision machining. He prefers projects with a clear experimental validation component rather than purely simulation-based studies. His doctoral student Luka Perović is available for extended industrial placements.
